hlp_start.en:
Macro Manager runs hotkey macros for you. Each macro has a trigger key; while you hold it (inside the chosen application) the macro plays.

- Tick a macro in the list to turn it on, untick to turn it off.
- The switch All macros in the banner turns every macro on or off at once.
- Dark mode switches the look of the app.
- The language button in the banner switches the app language (English, Čeština, Polski, Deutsch). The app restarts to apply it.
- Double-click a row (or press Edit) to change a macro. Add creates a new one, Copy duplicates it, Delete removes it.
- To select several macros drag the mouse over the rows (or Ctrl / Shift + click). Copy, Delete, Export, Move up / down and dragging out of the window work on all selected rows.
- Closing the window keeps the app running in the tray. Right-click the tray icon for Open window / Uninstall / Exit.
- The app always runs as administrator, so macros also work in games that run elevated.
- The search box above the list shows only the macros whose name, key or application contains the text. The cross next to it clears it.
ctx: HELP TOPIC TEXT (shown in the Help window, read as a manual)

hlp_edit.en:
Name - any text, shown in the list.
Profiles - which profiles the macro belongs to (can be several).
Trigger key - click the box, then press the key or a mouse button (right, middle, side buttons X1 / X2, mouse wheel). Hold Ctrl / Shift / Alt while pressing to make a combination, for example Ctrl+XButton1. Esc cancels.
Toggle - optional key that turns this macro on/off without opening the window. Backspace clears it.
Only in app (exe) - the macro works only while that program is in front. Press Select to pick a running application or browse for the .exe. Empty = works everywhere.
Type - Move + actions, Sequence or Script (.ahk). See the next topics.
Press - how the trigger key has to be pressed. Normal: the macro starts as soon as the key goes down. Short tap: a quick press and release - the macro plays once after the release. Double tap: press the key twice quickly. Long press: hold the key for a moment (with Repeat it keeps playing while you hold it). One key can carry up to three macros this way: short tap, double tap and long press. A Normal macro on the same key takes the whole key. Mouse wheel macros always start at once.
Run - Once per key press: plays one pass and waits until you release the key. Repeat while key is held: plays again and again until you release the key (it stops immediately). Not offered for Short tap - it always plays once.
Exact delays (bottom left) - the delays are kept to about a millisecond. On for new macros. Off = the older timing, where short delays often last 10-15 ms longer than written.

Save stores the macro, Cancel throws changes away.

hlp_move.en:
Made for games where you keep moving (for example A and D) and cast spells in between.

Directions - the movement keys, in order, for example: a,d
Actions in order - the keys to press, one per cycle, for example: 1,2,1,F7,1,F8

Every cycle does this, with the delays you set:
  1. direction down
  2. (delay 1) action down
  3. (delay 2) direction up
  4. (delay 3) action up
  5. (delay 4) pause, then the next direction + next action

The lists repeat from the start when they end. If Directions is empty, only the actions are pressed: hold time = delay 2, pause = delay 4.
If a game ignores the macro, raise the delays (20-30 ms is common).
ctx: HELP TOPIC TEXT (shown in the Help window, read as a manual)

hlp_seq.en:
A free list of steps. Write one step per line:

  down KEY PAUSE   - press and hold the key
  up KEY PAUSE     - release the key
  tap KEY PAUSE    - press and release at once

PAUSE is the wait after the step in milliseconds (empty = 0).

Example - quick A / D change:
  down a 25
  up a 5
  down d 25
  up d 5

Example - attack and spells:
  tap 1 600
  tap e 100
  tap F7 100

Example - two keys together:
  tap Shift+4 50

With Run = Repeat the lines play in a loop while the trigger key is held; with Once they play one time.
Keys that are still held when you release the trigger are released automatically.

hlp_script.en:
For anything the other types can not do. Paste or write your own AutoHotkey v2 script.

- The script runs as its own process while the macro is ticked, and is stopped when you untick it.
- It must be AutoHotkey v2 code (v1 scripts will not work).
- Trigger key and application filter are not used, your script does that itself.
- Imported .ahk files that were not made by Macro Manager become Script macros.
- An imported script asks before it runs for the first time: it runs with administrator rights, so only turn it on if you trust where it came from. The window shows what the script does (for example starts programs or deletes files) and offers to show the code.
ctx: HELP TOPIC TEXT (shown in the Help window, read as a manual)

hlp_keys.en:
Key names are the AutoHotkey names: a, 1, F7, Space, Enter, Tab, LCtrl, LShift, Numpad1 ...
A key can also be written as a scan code, for example sc002 - this is the physical key, regardless of layout. Keys like comma, plus, & and | are saved this way automatically.

Mouse: the trigger, toggle and All macros keys can also be a mouse button: RButton, MButton (wheel click), XButton1 / XButton2 (the two side buttons), or the wheel itself (WheelUp / WheelDown / WheelLeft / WheelRight). A wheel has no hold, so wheel macros always play once. The left button is not offered.
Gaming / MMO mice: windows only knows five mouse buttons, the extra side buttons are handled by the mouse software (G HUB, Synapse, iCUE, ...). Set them there to keys, best F13 - F24 (or Ctrl+Alt+number); Macro Manager then sees them as ordinary keys, so click the trigger box and press the side button.

Record (next to Directions and Actions): press Record, press the keys in the order you want, then press Done. The field fills in live. Macros are paused while recording.

Keys at the same time: keys that you hold together are saved as one step joined with +, for example Shift+4. When the macro plays, all of them go down together and are released together (not Shift first and 4 afterwards).
The same works by typing it in the fields: a,Shift+4,d

hlp_profiles.en:
Profiles keep different sets of macros apart (for example one per game).

- The profile button in the banner shows the current profile. Click it to switch, or to create / rename / delete a profile.
- The list shows only the macros of the current profile, and only those are active.
- In the editor, Profiles lets you choose one or more profiles for the macro. When you change a macro that belongs to several profiles, the app asks: apply the change to all of them, or only to the current profile (the other profiles keep the old version).
- Tick state of a macro stays the same in every profile; switching profile just changes which macros are in play.
- Deleting a profile moves macros that belonged only to it to the first remaining profile.

hlp_toggle.en:
Toggle (in the editor) - a key that switches that single macro on / off, same as ticking it in the list. A small tooltip shows ON / OFF.
All macros toggle key (button under the list) - switches the master switch. Works in every profile.

Click the button, press the key. Esc cancels, Backspace removes the key.
Macros of other profiles do not react to their toggle keys.

hlp_order.en:
Move up / Move down change the order in the list. Clicking a column header sorts the list (click again to reverse).

Export... saves the selected macro as a standalone AutoHotkey v2 .ahk file that also runs by itself (it asks for admin rights).
Import... loads one or more .ahk files (or just drag them onto the main window). You can also drag a macro from the list onto the desktop / a folder / a chat window to export it as an .ahk file. The macro is named after the file; files made by Macro Manager come back as editable macros, other scripts become Script macros. Imports go to the current profile and start switched off.
Export all... writes every macro to a folder, one file each.

Backup... (next to Uninstall) saves everything - macros, profiles, settings and script files - into one .mmbackup file, and restores it on a new PC or after a reinstall. You can also drop the backup file onto the window. Before restoring, the current state is saved as config\backup-before-restore.mmbackup.

hlp_updates.en:
The arrow icon in the banner (next to the profile button) shows whether a new version exists: grey = you are up to date, green = a new version is available. Hover it for details.

The app checks a few seconds after it starts (can be turned off in the tray menu: Check for updates at start). Click the icon at any time to check again. Nothing is installed until you click the green icon and confirm.

When you update, the app downloads the new file, checks its checksum, keeps the old one as Macro Manager.ahk.bak and restarts. Your macros, profiles and settings are stored separately in the config folder and stay exactly as they are.

If something goes wrong, close the app, delete Macro Manager.ahk and rename Macro Manager.ahk.bak back to Macro Manager.ahk.

The update needs internet access to github.com.

hlp_hub.en:
Macro Hub (the button next to the search box) shows macros shared by players. It opens as a panel on the side of the main window.

- Players' macros: macros of other players. My macros: the macros you shared, with their ratings and downloads.
- Search with words from the name, the game or the author: every word must match. 4story finds all 4Story macros, 4story war only the warrior ones.
- The game button filters one game, the sort button sorts by Top rated, Newest or Most downloaded.
- Every macro shows its average rating in stars (1 = worst, 5 = best) with the number of ratings in brackets, its author, its game, its trigger key and how many times it was downloaded.
- Download (or a double-click) adds the macro to the current profile, switched off. Check its key and application, then tick it.
- Rate gives 1 to 5 stars - one rating per installation, you can change it later. Your own macros can't be rated.
- Report sends a macro to be checked, for example a farm / AFK macro, which is not allowed. After several reports it is hidden.
- Delete (My macros) removes a macro you shared from Macro Hub; your own copy in the list stays.

Sharing: click the share icon at the end of a row in the main list, then fill in the name, the game, a description and your nickname. The icon turns gold once the macro is shared. Macros downloaded from Macro Hub show a download arrow instead and can be shared only after you change them.

Updates: when you change a macro you shared, the app asks whether to update it in Macro Hub - its ratings and downloads stay (until then its icon has a dot; click it to update). When the author updates a macro you downloaded, a notice appears and its arrow in the list turns green: click it to see what changed and take the new version or keep yours. Shared: keys, delays, Run and Press settings and the application. Not shared: the toggle key and your profiles. Script macros can't be shared.

Macro Hub needs internet access. Nobody can see who rated or reported a macro.

hlp_tips.en:
- The game does nothing: try raising the delays, make sure Only in app matches the game (use Select), and keep the app as administrator.
- Character runs in one direction: keep direction pairs in Directions (a,d) and the delay between cycles small but not 0.
- A macro does not start: check that it is ticked, All macros is on, it is in the current profile and the trigger key is set (not undefined).
- Two macros with the same trigger key: only one of them works - use different keys, different profiles or different Press modes (short tap / double tap / long press).
- Macros made before Exact delays existed keep their old timing. If you switch Exact delays on for one of them, it may play faster - then raise its delays a little.
- Stuck key after an abort: press and release it once; the app releases keys it pressed when the macro stops.
- Settings and scripts live in the config folder next to the app.
